title: Spontaneous symmetry-breaking in equilibrium tree-packing configurations of a kinetically constrained cubic-lattice system
abstract: We explore kinetic-constraint induced thermodynamic phase transition in the cubic lattice, employing the Fredrikson-Anderson spin model with hyperparameter $K=2$ as a representative kinetic system. Each lattice site may flip its binary occupation state if at most one of its six nearest neighbors is currently occupied. The whole set of microscopic configurations that are kinetically connected with the fully empty one is described by an equilibrium partition function with a single global constraint, that is, the occupied sites do not form closed loops but instead organize into different tree components in the lattice. We discover a continuous thermodynamic gas--crystal phase transition in the cubic system and determine the critical chemical potential $μ^* \approx -3.252$, at which the occupied sites of the equilibrium tree-packing configurations start to prefer one of the two nested cubic sublattices. This thermodynamic phase transition is absent in the two-dimensional square lattice.
summary: This paper analyzes the phase transitions in a kinetically constrained cubic lattice where occupied sites must form tree structures. Using Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size-scaling, the authors identify a continuous gas-crystal transition in 3D at $\mu^* \approx -3.252$. This transition, marked by spontaneous symmetry-breaking, is absent in the 2D square lattice, highlighting the critical role of spatial dimensionality.
main_problem: The study investigates spontaneous symmetry-breaking and thermodynamic phase transitions in equilibrium tree-packing configurations within a kinetically constrained cubic lattice.
main_result: A continuous gas–crystal phase transition is found in the 3D cubic lattice at $\mu^* \approx -3.252$, leading to spontaneous symmetry-breaking between two nested sublattices, a transition absent in the 2D square lattice.
method: The research employs numerical simulations, including Markov-Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) dynamics and finite-size-scaling (FSS) analysis, to determine critical parameters.
model_or_system: The system is a cubic lattice governed by the Fredrikson-Anderson spin model with a kinetic constraint ($K=2$), ensuring occupied sites form tree components. The thermodynamic properties are analyzed via a partition function constrained by the absence of occupied loops.
key_observables: Mean occupation density ($ho$), magnetization order parameter ($m$), and the absolute magnetization $|m|$ are key observables used to detect phase transitions.
important_parameters: The critical chemical potential $\mu^* \approx -3.252$ and the lattice dimension (3D cubic vs. 2D square) are crucial parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system reaches equilibrium and relies on finite-size-scaling theory to extrapolate critical points.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of density and magnetization on the chemical potential $\mu$, showing characteristic changes indicative of a phase transition in 3D but not in 2D.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system's behavior by first establishing the model and constraints, then applying MCMC simulations to measure observables like magnetization, and finally using FSS analysis to pinpoint the critical point and compare dimensionality effects.
why_interesting: The study provides a concrete example of how kinetic constraints can induce rich thermodynamic behavior, offering insights into the interplay between local dynamics and global phase transitions, which is relevant for understanding complex quantum many-body systems.
